 1.
The petitioner is an accused in connection with Sambalpur Town P.S. Case No.227 of 2024 corresponding to G.R. Case No.1350 of 2024 registered for the alleged commission of offences punishable under Sections 419/420/468/471/109/120-B of IPC, pending in the Court of the learned SDJM, Sambalpur.

The petitioner had approached the learned SDJM, Sambalpur in G.R. Case No.
1350 of 2024 praying for grant of bail.
The learned court below vide its order dated 29.03.2025 rejected the bail application of the petitioner.
Thereafter, the petitioner approached the learned Sessions Judge, Sambalpur in BLAPL No. 195 of 2025 praying for bail.
The learned court below vide its order dated 07.04.2025 rejected the bail application of the petitioner.
Being aggrieved, the petitioner has filed the present application under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. praying for enlargement of on bail.
2. The petitioner is working as a District Sub-Registrar.
The petitioner name has not been mentioned in the FIR.

The prime co-accused persons those names found mentioned in the FIR and other co-accused persons, i.e, seller, purchaser and facilitator, have already been enlarged on anticipatory bail by this Court.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner, on instruction from the petitioner, submits that, except the present bail application, no other bail application of the petitioner is pending in any other Court Surya Narayan Samal vs State Of Odisha ....

4.

The prosecution case is that F.I.R. was lodged by the informant alleging therein that one Govinda Meher sold the land as the recorded owner, namely, Binod Kumar Gupta, the brother of the complainant to Sujit Kumar Patra and Venkat Balaji Patra vide Regd. Sale Deed No.11622204828 dated 23.09.2022 in the office of the District Sub-Registrar, Sambalpur.
Thereafter, the said purchasers have also prepared the RoR in their names vide M.S. Khata No.733/4708.

It is further alleged that the photograph and signature affixed in the aforesaid Sale Deed is not the photograph and signature of the original recorded land owner-tenant, i.e., brother of the complainant.

Hence,
the FIR.

5. Mr. Dhal, learned Senior Advocate has handed over the order dated 27.03.2025 passed in ABLAPL No.2494 of 2025 in regard to Chandra Prasad Dunguria and another and order dated 23.04.2025 passed in ABLAPL No.10840 of 2024 in regard to Binod Kumar Gupta.
6. Perusal of the aforementioned orders reveal that the accused persons those who have been enlarged on anticipatory bail are the prime accused persons.
The petitioner was employed as a Sub-Registrar before whom the offending documents were allegedly registered.
Therefore, he is entitled to bail.

7. Mr. S.N. Biswal, learned Addl. Standing Counsel submits that indeed few of the co-accused persons have been enlarged on anticipatory bail, however, pre-arrest bail of principal accused Sujit Kumar Patra and V. Balaji Patra has been rejected by this Court on 04.10.2024 in ABLAPL No 10828 of 2024.
The petitioner being a government servant and his name has not been mentioned in the FIR and the petitioner is in custody since 29.03.2025, he is entitled to bail.
8. Regard being had to the fact that the co-accused persons have already been enlarged on anticipatory bail granted by this Court, as mentioned above and the petitioner, who is a govt.
Employee is in custody since 29.03.2025, I am inclined to enlarge the accused- Petitioner on bail.

In the event, the petitioner is found wanting for violation of any of the bail conditions imposed by this Court or the trial Court even on a single occasion, the prosecution is at liberty to move Surya Narayan Samal vs State Of Odisha ....
